text: Which ghost is stunned by a smudge stick for 180 seconds — twice as long as any other?
detail: Burn a smudge near its room and you get an unusually long quiet period.
explain: Spirit has no offensive abilities — its defining feature is its weakness to smudge sticks. A smudge stun lasts 180 s for a Spirit versus 90 s for the average ghost. If you smudge and the ghost goes silent for 3 minutes, you've almost certainly got a Spirit.

text: You smudge a ghost in its room. It doesn't hunt again for over three minutes. Most likely?
detail: Standard smudge silence is 90 seconds. This was much longer.
explain: Spirit's smudge stun lasts 180 s. It's one of the cleanest identification tests in the game — if you can spare a smudge in the ghost's room and time the silence, the answer comes back fast.

text: You place salt in a doorway the ghost has crossed multiple times. The salt remains perfectly undisturbed. Which ghost?
detail: Footstep sounds confirmed it walked over the salt — but nothing was kicked up.
explain: Wraith is the only ghost that never disturbs salt. It can fly/teleport through environments, bypassing physical materials. Salt placed in a confirmed patrol path remaining untouched is one of the cleanest Wraith confirmations in the game.

text: EMF readings keep appearing far from the ghost's favorite room, near random players. The ghost room is on the second floor; the readings are in the basement.
detail: It seems to be appearing in two places at once.
explain: Wraith can teleport directly adjacent to a random player, leaving an EMF reading at the new location. Far-from-room EMF spikes near players are a Wraith hallmark — keep a crucifix on you, not on the floor.

text: You snap a photo of the manifesting ghost. It vanishes from sight but the event keeps running — singing continues, lights still flicker.
detail: The ghost is gone but the chaos isn't.
explain: Phantom disappears visually when photographed, but the surrounding ghost event keeps playing out. It also stays invisible longer than other ghosts during hunts, making it especially hard to loop visually.

text: Looking directly at the ghost causes your sanity to plummet much faster than usual. Which ghost?
detail: Eye contact is shockingly expensive.
explain: Phantom drains 0.5% sanity per second when you look at it during a hunt or event, well above the standard rate. The flash-then-vanish photo trick is the textbook counter; otherwise, avert your gaze.

text: The ghost throws multiple objects from a pile simultaneously — and your sanity tanks every time it does.
detail: Several small items have just left the table in one motion.
explain: Poltergeist's signature is the multi-throw. It can hurl multiple objects at once and drains sanity from nearby players each time. To test, pile several small items in the ghost room — Poltergeists love a target-rich environment.

text: Compared to other ghosts, this one launches objects with much more force — across the room rather than just nudging them.
detail: Standard ghosts throw with force value 1–3. This one throws harder.
explain: Poltergeist applies force 2–6 on thrown objects versus the standard 1–3, and during hunts it throws every 0.5 s rather than rolling a 50% chance per interaction. If small objects are flying across rooms with serious velocity, suspect a Poltergeist.

text: The ghost is locked on one player and won't leave them alone. Other teammates can walk right past during a hunt unbothered.
detail: It fixated on a single investigator the moment you stepped inside.
explain: Banshee picks one target at the start of the contract and only hunts based on that player's sanity, not the team average. Non-targets can move freely around the ghost during a chase — a unique behavior used by experienced teams to bait safely.

text: The Parabolic Microphone at the front of the location picks up a piercing scream — exclusive to one ghost type.
detail: It's not a paranormal whisper or growl — it's a clean scream.
explain: Banshee has a unique scream that the Parabolic Microphone has a roughly 33% chance of picking up. No other ghost produces this sound. If your mic captures one, you can confirm the ghost type without even setting foot inside.

text: Three teammates are at 80% sanity, one is at 30%. The ghost only hunts when targeting the low-sanity player. Which ghost?
detail: Team sanity isn't the trigger — one specific player's is.
explain: Banshee uses only its target's sanity for hunt calculations, ignoring the team average entirely. If hunts only start when one specific player drops low, you're hunting a Banshee.

text: When the breaker is on, this ghost is dramatically faster. It will never, under any circumstances, switch the breaker off itself.
detail: Cut the power and it slows immediately.
explain: Jinn draws strength from electricity. With the breaker on and line of sight from at least 3 m away, it accelerates to 2.5 m/s. It has a hard rule against turning the breaker off itself, so if you witness the ghost cutting power, rule out Jinn immediately.

text: An EMF reader left on the fuse box keeps firing even when no one is near it. Sanity also drops sharply for anyone standing close to the ghost room.
detail: The breaker is becoming an unexpected hotspot.
explain: Jinn can zap a nearby player for an instant 25% sanity drop, which generates an EMF reading at the fuse box. Leaving an EMF reader there is a clean Jinn-detection trick.

text: You're at 55% sanity. Lights are off. The ghost hunts. Lights on, it didn't hunt until you dropped below 40%. Which ghost?
detail: Hunt threshold seems to swing with the lighting.
explain: Mare's threshold is 60% with lights off and 40% with lights on. Keeping the breaker on and rooms lit is the single best counter — Mare also turns off lights you've just switched on within 4 m.

text: A ghost that actively turns lights OFF, prefers dark rooms during roaming, and will never turn a light on.
detail: Walk into the room and the bulb pops out.
explain: Mare prefers darkness. It can switch off any light you turned on within 4 m of itself, with a 10-second cooldown on the ability. To test, turn on lights in adjacent rooms but leave one dark — the Mare should drift toward the unlit one.

text: A hunt starts. With line of sight, the ghost is impossibly fast — 3 m/s. The moment you hide, footsteps slow to a crawl.
detail: Speed extremes: there's no middle setting.
explain: Revenant's defining mechanic is the speed contrast — 3 m/s when it sees or hears you, 1 m/s the moment you hide. The change is dramatic and unmistakable. The correct play is always: hide immediately, never run.

text: Which ghost should you NEVER attempt to outrun?
detail: Running in line of sight is a death sentence — hiding is the only correct response.
explain: Revenant in chase mode moves at 3 m/s — faster than the player walk speed. You cannot outrun it in a straight line. The only viable defense is breaking line of sight before it locks on, then hiding silently until its speed drops.

text: Lowest hunt threshold of any ghost in the game?
detail: This ghost is so passive it almost ignores you.
explain: Shade sits at 35% sanity — the lowest base hunt threshold in the game. Thaye can technically dip to 15% at full age, but its base threshold starts at 75%. For default-state ghosts, Shade is the floor.

text: Multiple players stand in the ghost room. The ghost refuses to interact with anything until they leave.
detail: Activity goes dead the moment anyone walks in.
explain: Shade is the most passive ghost in the game. It won't generate evidence or interact with objects while a player is in the same room — and it can't initiate a hunt above 35% sanity. The counter is to leave the room and monitor it remotely via camera.

text: It's been 30 minutes. Sanity is at 40%. Still no hunt. Which ghost should you start strongly suspecting?
detail: A patient, shy spirit.
explain: Shade's 35% threshold means a long hunt-free stretch even at low sanity is a major Shade indicator. It also has a 0% chance to trigger ghost events at 100% sanity, with that chance scaling up by 2% per percentage point of sanity lost.

text: At what sanity does a Demon start hunting?
detail: All other ghosts cap out at 60% or below for their hunt threshold (situational cases aside).
explain: Demon hunts at 70% sanity. It's the only ghost with a base threshold above the standard 50% (Yokai and Thaye can go higher under specific conditions). If you're being hunted in the green sanity range, suspect Demon first.

text: The crucifix radius for one ghost is 50% larger than normal — but smudges only stun it for 60 seconds.
detail: Cross is bigger, smoke is shorter.
explain: Demon has a 50% larger crucifix radius (5 m vs 3 m) but its smudge stun is only 60 s versus the standard 90 s. The crucifix is your friend, the smudge stick less so. Always carry one from the start on Demon-possible contracts.

text: You just unlocked the front door. The ghost initiates a hunt within 30 seconds of entry, while everyone is still at 100% sanity.
detail: No sanity drain. No warning. Just an immediate hunt.
explain: Demon can initiate hunts at any sanity level (with low probability) on top of its 70% threshold. Coupled with a 20-second hunt cooldown (vs standard 25), it's the only ghost that can credibly attack you the moment you walk in.

text: Sanity is dropping 15% faster than expected. There's an open door in the ghost room, and players are within 7.5 m. Which ghost?
detail: The door, not the ghost, seems to be the trigger.
explain: Yurei drains 15% sanity in a 7.5 m radius when there's an open door in its current room. Keep doors open to encourage this ability and confirm it. Smudging a Yurei traps it in its favorite room for 90 seconds — a useful side test.

text: A door in the ghost room opens, then closes, on its own. An EMF reader picks up two separate level-2 readings on that door.
detail: The door isn't being slammed — it's being deliberately moved through.
explain: Yurei can fully open or close doors, and each action generates two EMF 2 readings on the door itself. Combined with rapid sanity drain via open doors, it's one of the more recognizable behavioral signatures.

text: This ghost is unusually visible during hunts — manifesting longer and more frequently than others — and it NEVER appears in mist form.
detail: Lots of activity. Almost never subtle.
explain: Oni is the most physically visible ghost during hunts. It manifests in full body during events rather than as mist or shadow, and is more active when players are nearby — opposite of the Shade. Stay close to the ghost room and use a camera to spot it.

text: Object throws are unusually forceful AND the ghost is more active when players are nearby — but it isn't a Poltergeist.
detail: It's an active ghost with stronger-than-normal throws, full-body manifestations, and never mist.
explain: Oni throws with elevated force similar to Poltergeists but is identified by its visibility, full-body manifestations, never appearing as mist, and its preference for being active around players rather than alone.

text: You're at 75% sanity. You speak into voice chat near the ghost. A hunt starts. Which ghost?
detail: Talking near the ghost just raised its hunt threshold.
explain: Yokai raises its hunt threshold to 80% — the highest situational threshold in the game — when players talk within 2 m of it. Without voice chat nearby, it's a standard 50%. Hunts above 70% with voice activity = Yokai before Demon.

text: During a hunt, this ghost can only hear players within 2.5 m of itself — much shorter than the standard 9 m range.
detail: Stay silent and it'll walk right past.
explain: Yokai's hearing range during hunts is reduced to 2.5 m, versus the standard 9 m. If you're hiding without line of sight and using global chat doesn't seem to draw it, suspect Yokai. Test by speaking on the B key during a hunt.

text: With the breaker OFF, the ghost moves at full speed and emits visible frost breath during hunts. With the breaker ON, it slows noticeably in warm rooms.
detail: Cold air makes it faster.
explain: Hantu scales speed with room temperature: faster in cold rooms, slower in warm ones. With the breaker off, all rooms stay cold and it runs at full speed. Visible frost breath during hunts is a unique Hantu tell — no other ghost shows it.

text: During a hunt you can SEE the ghost breathing out visible frost — even though that's not normally a feature.
detail: It exhales clouds of frozen air mid-chase.
explain: Hantu is the only ghost that visibly exhales frost during hunts, an effect tied to its cold-affinity mechanic. Combined with its tendency to trip the breaker more often than most ghosts, frost breath is a reliable visual ID.

text: The D.O.T.S. silhouette is visible ONLY through the video camera — never to the naked eye when you're standing outside the room.
detail: Look directly through the doorway: nothing. Look through the camera: there it is.
explain: Goryo only displays D.O.T.S. through a video camera, and only when no player is in the same room. Walk-by D.O.T.S. is not a Goryo. If you can see it on the monitor but not through a doorway, you've got one.

text: On a large map, the ghost almost never leaves a small area near its favorite room — even on contracts with high roaming settings.
detail: It's strangely homebound.
explain: Goryo rarely roams far from its favorite room. On limited-evidence runs, D.O.T.S. Projector is always one of its guaranteed evidences — combined with its homebound behavior, you can often confirm it with just a camera and patience.

text: During a hunt, footsteps and electronic flicker arrive almost simultaneously — meaning by the time your flashlight stutters, it's already extremely close.
detail: Audio range is shorter than usual. Visual range is normal.
explain: Myling footsteps only audible within 12 m versus the standard 20 m, while electronics still flicker at 10 m. The 'lantern test' uses this: by the time you hear it, your flashlight already warned you. Quietest hunter in the game.

text: Despite being a quieter ghost during hunts, this one is unusually CHATTY on the Parabolic Microphone — paranormal sounds every 40–60 seconds.
detail: Loud on the mic, quiet on its feet.
explain: Myling produces paranormal sounds at the highest frequency in the game — roughly every 40–60 s on the Parabolic Microphone versus 80+ seconds for most ghosts. It's a paradox: noisy when idle, near-silent when hunting.

text: What's the Onryo's standard hunt threshold?
detail: Slightly elevated from average, but not as extreme as the Demon.
explain: Onryo hunts at 60% sanity by default. This is higher than the standard 50% but lower than the Demon's 70%. The threshold can also be bypassed entirely by extinguishing three of its candles in succession.

text: This ghost is repelled by fire. If you blow out three of its candles in succession, it attempts a hunt — regardless of sanity.
detail: Flames are its kryptonite, but extinguishing them is also a trigger.
explain: Onryo is afraid of fire but every time a flame is extinguished near it, it counts up — three in a row triggers an attempted hunt. If a fourth lit flame is in range, it acts as a one-time crucifix and blocks the hunt. Keep at least three flames lit at all times.

text: Two ghost interactions trigger almost simultaneously — one within 3 m of the favorite room, another 16 m away in a totally different area.
detail: It can't be in two places at once. Or can it?
explain: The Twins interact with objects in two locations near-simultaneously: standard 3 m radius for the main interaction and an extended 16 m radius for the decoy. There aren't actually two ghosts — temperature drops and evidence only appear in the real room.

text: Comparing two consecutive hunts, the ghost's speed feels slightly different — one hunt at ~1.45 m/s, the next at ~1.87 m/s.
detail: Subtle ±10% variation between hunts.
explain: The Twins alternate which twin initiates hunts — one is 10% slower than baseline (1.45 m/s), the other 10% faster (1.87 m/s). The slower twin spawns in the favorite room, the faster one in a random room. Watching hunt-to-hunt speed shifts is the cleanest behavioral tell.

text: Raiju's hunt threshold near active electronics?
detail: Standard ghosts hunt at 50%. Raiju gets a boost when surrounded by electronics.
explain: Raiju hunts at 65% when active electronics are nearby, versus 50% standard. The counter is simple: turn off everything non-essential (cameras, EMF readers, sound recorders) during a hunt to deny it the bonus.

text: This ghost accelerates to 2.5 m/s when it's near active electronics — and electronics within ~10 m on the same floor blow out around it during hunts.
detail: It feeds off your gear.
explain: Raiju draws power from electronics. Near active gear it hits 2.5 m/s, and its interference radius scales by map size — 6 m small, 8 m medium, 10 m large. During a Raiju hunt, expect cameras and flashlights to die early.

text: You find a SIX-fingered handprint on a wall. Which ghost is this conclusive proof of?
detail: An extra finger. Definitely not human.
explain: Obake is the only ghost in the game that can leave a six-fingered handprint. Other unique prints: 2 fingerprints on a light switch (vs 1 standard) and 5 on a keyboard or prison door (vs 4 standard).

text: Fingerprints from this ghost have a 75% chance to appear instead of the usual 100%, and they fade noticeably faster than other ghosts'.
detail: Don't rule out fingerprints from a single failed check.
explain: Obake has a 75% chance of leaving UV evidence on interactions versus the standard 100%, and its prints decay faster. If your team can't get fingerprints in a single sweep, run UV again — Obake is the most likely culprit.

text: The ghost's behavior shifts dramatically every minute or two — speed, hunting patterns, event style. Then halfway through the contract it just acts like a totally different ghost.
detail: Two minutes ago it was a Spirit. Now it's a Hantu. Pick one.
explain: The Mimic copies another ghost's abilities, speed, hunt thresholds, and event preferences, switching every 30 s – 2 min (but never during a hunt). It cannot copy evidence — that's where you catch it.

text: The contract clearly shows three confirmed evidences, BUT Ghost Orbs also keep appearing on camera even though they aren't listed.
detail: The fourth orb shouldn't be there.
explain: The Mimic always produces Ghost Orbs as a 'fake' fourth piece of evidence, regardless of its actual evidence set. Spotting orbs alongside evidence that should exclude them is the cleanest Mimic identification.

text: After getting a Spirit Box response, your sanity starts draining twice as fast. Sanity pills clear it; entering a lit room does not.
detail: The ghost cursed you for asking questions.
explain: Moroi curses any player who receives a Spirit Box response or hears one through a Parabolic Microphone, doubling their sanity drain rate. Only sanity pills remove the curse. Incense also weakens it for longer than standard.

text: At low team sanity with line of sight, this ghost hits 3.7 m/s — the fastest hunt speed in the game.
detail: Faster than the Revenant. Speed scales with sanity loss.
explain: Moroi scales speed with the team's average sanity. At 0% sanity with line of sight, it reaches 3.7 m/s — faster than any other ghost. Compare hunt speed early vs late in the contract; a dramatic increase is Moroi's signature.

text: Deogen's hunt threshold?
detail: Slightly lower than the standard, but not as low as Shade.
explain: Deogen hunts at 40% sanity. Slightly lower than the standard 50%. Despite this it's far from passive — its real terror is that it can always find you.

text: Hiding is useless against this ghost. It sprints toward you from across the map — and then slows to a crawl when it gets within a few meters of you.
detail: It always knows where you are, but it's painfully slow up close.
explain: Deogen always knows player locations during hunts. It moves at 3 m/s from a distance but drops to 0.4 m/s within 2.5 m of you — the slowest any ghost moves in the game. Loop around objects or walk slowly to survive.

text: Standing within 1 m of the ghost and using the Spirit Box, you hear a distinctive heavy, bull-like breathing sound.
detail: It's not a voice. It's a heavy exhale.
explain: Deogen has a 33% chance to produce a heavy breathing response on the Spirit Box when you're within 1 m. The sound is exclusive to Deogen and a near-certain confirmation.

text: What's Thaye's INITIAL hunt threshold at age 0?
detail: Highest base threshold among all ghosts.
explain: Thaye starts at 75% hunt threshold (higher than even the Demon's 70%), but decreases by 6 per age increment. By age 10, the threshold sits at just 15% — the lowest possible threshold in the game.

text: The ghost was hyperactive at the start of the contract — hunting early, interacting constantly. Thirty minutes later it's slower, less aggressive, almost docile.
detail: Aging in reverse, in a sense.
explain: Thaye ages every 1–2 minutes while a player is in the same room (longer if empty). Each age increment slows it down and lowers its hunt threshold. The dramatic activity drop-off is its signature — identify it fast, before evidence becomes hard to find.

text: What item can reveal Thaye's current age?
detail: Cursed possessions sometimes give game-mechanic info.
explain: Ouija Board can reveal Thaye's current age. Each age increment adds 1–4 to the displayed 'human age,' so a freshly aged Thaye reads younger than a heavily aged one. It's the only ghost where the Ouija gives you a usable mechanic readout.

text: This ghost gets STRONGER when players move around close to it — and weakens significantly when they stand still.
detail: Movement provokes. Stillness pacifies.
explain: Dayan reacts sharply to player movement up close. The cleanest tell is the stand-still test: once you know it's nearby, freeze completely. If activity 'softens,' it's a Dayan. During hunts, it speeds up when you move and slows when you stop.

text: During hunts, this ghost's speed seems to react to YOUR movement — faster when you move, slower when you stop.
detail: Stillness slows it. Motion accelerates it.
explain: Dayan is one of the newer ghosts (Winter 2025), and its movement-responsive speed is its core identifier. Unlike Revenant (LOS-based) or Aswang (also LOS), Dayan keys off your actual motion. Stand still in a safe spot during a hunt to test.

text: Using crucifixes and smudges seems to PROVOKE this ghost, and your protective tools feel less effective as the contract progresses — until it suddenly seems to exhaust itself.
detail: Defense becomes offense, then offense exhausts itself.
explain: Gallu reacts to protective equipment. Crucifixes and smudges provoke it and become less effective over time as it 'rages.' Once it's enraged enough, it exhausts itself and your tools work again — a 'worse → better' cycle that's its unique tell.

text: The ghost flips between two distinct moods on the same contract — early hunts feel Demon-like, then the same ghost goes slow and easy to track, almost Shade-like.
detail: Two personalities, one ghost.
explain: Obambo alternates between an aggressive state (earlier, faster hunts, sometimes reported above 70% sanity) and a calm state (slower hunts, easier to track). The dual-state behavior tricks newer hunters into calling it a Shade or an Oni.

text: This ghost is functionally BLIND but has exceptional hearing. Stand silent and motionless during a hunt and it will walk right past you.
detail: Don't breathe. Don't crouch. Don't touch a single button.
explain: Kormos (added May 2026) translates roughly to 'one who does not see.' It's blind but has heightened hearing — the stand-still-and-silent test is the most reliable ID. Equipment noise, footsteps, and voice all draw it in faster than any other ghost.

text: Kormos shares all three pieces of evidence with which other ghost — meaning you can't ID it on evidence alone?
detail: Same evidence trio: Ghost Orbs, Spirit Box, Ultraviolet.
explain: Kormos shares Ghost Orbs + Spirit Box + UV with The Mimic. If you collect that combo, you MUST behavior-test (stand-still vs orb-decoy) to distinguish them before submitting your guess.

text: This ghost accelerates significantly faster than normal when it has line of sight on a player — but it can also be lost more easily once you break that sight.
detail: Chase mode is the danger; search mode is forgiving.
explain: Aswang (added May 2026) gains acceleration faster than other ghosts when it sees you, but prefers chasing over searching. Break line of sight as often as possible — its threat level drops sharply once it loses you.

text: Aswang vs Revenant — how do you tell them apart by speed mechanics?
detail: Both react to line of sight, but the curves differ.
options: Aswang has faster but more consistent acceleration during chases; Revenant has a massive speed jump with sight and a huge slow-down without
Aswang is always faster than Revenant at every distance
explain: Aswang's acceleration is smoother and more consistent, while Revenant has an extreme binary: 3 m/s with line of sight, 1 m/s without. Looking at the speed curve over a chase is the cleanest behavioral distinction.

text: Three teammates compare notes after a contract. They were hunted at 75% sanity. They were NOT talking near the ghost. Most likely?
detail: Hunt at 75% sanity rules out almost everything.
options: Either Demon or Obambo aggressive — Yokai needs voice nearby
explain: Demon hunts at 70%, Obambo's aggressive state has been reported above 70%, and Yokai needs talking within 2 m to reach its 80% threshold. With no voice nearby, you're picking between Demon and Obambo.

text: Smudge a ghost. It can't hunt for 60 seconds. What ghost is it likely to be?
detail: Standard smudge silence is 90 seconds. Spirit is 180. This was much shorter.
explain: Demon's smudge stun is just 60 s. Standard is 90 s; Spirit is 180 s. Smudge stick timing is one of the cleanest ways to distinguish these three.

text: You stay perfectly still and silent during a hunt. The ghost still finds you instantly. Which is it almost certainly NOT?
detail: What ghost would have been fooled by your discipline?
explain: Kormos is blind and relies on sound; staying motionless and silent should let it walk past. Deogen always knows your location regardless. Revenant uses line of sight and sound. Yokai has reduced hearing range. If perfect stealth failed, it isn't a Kormos.

text: Which ghost uses the SLOWEST hunt speed when adjacent to a player?
detail: It's a slow shuffle once it's right on top of you.
explain: Deogen drops to 0.4 m/s within 2.5 m of a player — the slowest speed any ghost achieves in the game. Aged Thaye and hidden-from Revenant both bottom out around 1 m/s.

text: Which ghost is the FASTEST possible during a hunt under perfect (worst) conditions?
detail: All speeds at maximum.
options: Moroi at 3.7 m/s at 0% sanity with LOS
explain: Moroi can hit 3.7 m/s at 0% team sanity with line of sight — the fastest possible ghost speed in the game. Revenant maxes at 3 m/s, Hantu around 2.7 m/s in cold rooms, Thaye starts at 2.75 m/s.

text: Which ghost can hunt above 50% sanity WITHOUT any special condition like voice chat or electronics?
detail: Pure baseline thresholds only.
explain: Only Demon has a baseline threshold above 50% (70%). Yokai needs voice within 2 m to reach 80%, Raiju needs active electronics for 65%, and Mare's 60% needs lights off in its room. Demon needs no trigger.

text: Salt remains undisturbed after the ghost crosses the room. Which is it?
detail: Footsteps confirm movement. Salt is untouched.
explain: Wraith is the only ghost that doesn't step in salt, owing to its ability to fly/teleport through environments. Untouched salt after confirmed ghost movement is a near-perfect ID.

text: Three identical contracts. In Contract A, hunts started at 50%. B started at 45%. C started at 35%. Most likely candidates for C?
detail: C started hunting unusually late.
options: Either Shade or Mare with lights on
explain: Shade hunts at 35% base. Mare with lights on hunts at 40%, very close to 35%. Both are plausible C ghosts. Demon (70%) and Yokai (50% baseline) would hunt much earlier.

text: Heavy bull-like breathing on the Spirit Box, only audible within 1 m of the ghost. Unique ID?
detail: It's not a voice, it's a respiratory sound.
explain: Deogen is the only ghost that produces a heavy-breathing response on the Spirit Box. You must be within 1 m and there's a 33% chance per question. Combined with the always-knows-you-location behavior, it's a quick ID.

text: Average sanity drain is doubled for a player who just got a Spirit Box response. What's happening?
detail: Sanity pills clear it. Standing in a lit room doesn't.
options: Yurei is draining everyone in 7.5 m
Moroi has cursed the player via Spirit Box
explain: Moroi applies a curse to any player who receives a Spirit Box response or hears one through a Parabolic Mic, doubling their sanity drain. Sanity pills are the only direct counter; ambient light won't fix it.

text: You leave a smudge stick burning in the ghost's room. The ghost is then 'locked' in that room for 90 seconds — can't roam out. Which ghost?
detail: Smudge as cage, not just stun.
explain: Yurei is uniquely trapped in its favorite room for 90 seconds after a smudge — it can't even leave to roam. This makes it easier to test other rooms safely after a smudge.

text: Below what sanity does the AVERAGE ghost begin hunting?
detail: Most ghosts share one common hunt threshold.
explain: 50% sanity is the standard hunt threshold for the majority of ghosts. The notable deviations — Demon 70%, Shade 35%, Mare 40/60, Deogen 40%, Onryo 60%, Yokai 50/80, Thaye 75→15, Raiju 50/65 — are easier to remember once you've memorized 50% as the baseline.

text: Most ghosts in Phasmophobia move at what base speed during a hunt?
detail: It's not the same as the player walk speed.
explain: Standard hunt speed is 1.7 m/s. Outliers include Revenant (3 m/s LOS / 1 m/s hidden), Moroi (up to 3.7 m/s), Deogen (3 m/s far → 0.4 m/s near), Jinn (2.5 m/s with breaker), Raiju (2.5 m/s near electronics), and aged Thaye (declining from 2.75 m/s).

text: A standard ghost hearing range during hunts is roughly how many meters?
detail: Yokai is the famous exception at 2.5 m.
explain: Standard hunt hearing range is roughly 9 m. Yokai narrows this to 2.5 m, while Kormos's hearing is functionally unlimited as long as you make any sound. Stay silent or move out to ~10 m to break a standard ghost's awareness.

text: Which ghost type uniquely shape-shifts between ghost models DURING a hunt?
detail: Watch the ghost flicker count.
explain: Obake shape-shifts model during hunts at very specific flicker counts (12th, 27th, 39th, 54th, 62nd, 80th, 105th, 120th, 132nd flickers per community testing). The Mimic copies behaviors and the Phantom disappears in photos, but model swaps mid-hunt = Obake.

text: What's the simplest one-test confirmation for a Wraith?
detail: Doesn't require risk during a hunt.
options: Salt in a doorway it crosses — remains undisturbed
Place a candle near its favorite room
explain: Wraith's clean test is salt in a confirmed patrol path. If the salt is undisturbed after the ghost has crossed it, you've got a Wraith. It's risk-free since you don't have to be near the ghost during a hunt.

text: Sanity drains FASTER in which one of these scenarios? (No cursed possession effects)
detail: All players have the same loadout. No items.
options: Standing within 7.5 m of a Yurei with an open door in its room
Standing in a fully lit room at 75% sanity
explain: Yurei causes a 15% sanity drop on all players within 7.5 m when there's an open door in its current room. This is on top of base passive drain. Closing doors and keeping out of range neutralizes it.

text: During a hunt, the ghost passes within meters of you while you're in voice chat — but turns away even though you're talking loudly.
detail: It didn't hear you despite the proximity.
options: Yokai (hearing range only 2.5 m during hunts)
explain: Yokai's hunt hearing radius shrinks to 2.5 m. If you talked from 4–5 m and it didn't react, that's the test. Kormos still hears noise, Deogen always knows, Phantom doesn't care about your voice.

text: Which two ghosts share EXACTLY the same three pieces of evidence?
detail: On evidence alone, you can't tell them apart.
options: Kormos & The Mimic — both Ghost Orbs / Spirit Box / UV
explain: Kormos and The Mimic both feature Ghost Orbs, Spirit Box, and UV. You MUST use behavior tests — Mimic shows ghost orbs as a decoy 4th evidence; Kormos ignores motionless, silent players during hunts.

text: What's the safest survival strategy when you suspect a Deogen?
detail: Hiding doesn't work.
options: Loop around objects or walk slowly down a long hallway as it approaches
Hide in the closest closet immediately
Run as far away as possible
Drop a smudge stick at your feet
explain: Deogen can always find you, so hiding is wasted. The correct play is to loop around an object or walk slowly down a long hallway. Once it's within 2.5 m it drops to 0.4 m/s — slower than a walking player. Maintain the gap and you survive.

text: Which ghost's hunt threshold can drop to just 15% — the lowest possible in the entire game?
detail: Only at maximum age.
explain: Thaye at age 10 hunts at 15% sanity — the lowest possible threshold in the game. Each age increment drops the threshold by 6, starting from 75%. Note that aged Thaye is also one of the slowest, so it becomes nearly inert.

text: What's the unique fingerprint signature on a LIGHT SWITCH that confirms one specific ghost?
detail: Other ghosts leave one print. This one leaves two.
options: Obake — 2 fingerprints on a light switch
Goryo — fingerprint visible only on camera
explain: Obake leaves 2 fingerprints on a light switch (other ghosts: 1) and 5 on a keyboard or prison door (other ghosts: 4). The six-fingered handprint is also exclusive to Obake.

text: The ghost throws an object that's MUCH further across the room than normal — but it's a single object, not multiple. Manifests in full body during events. Never appears as mist.
detail: Aggressive, visible, single-throws.
explain: Oni throws single objects with elevated force but doesn't multi-throw like a Poltergeist. Its distinguishing tells: full body manifestation in events, never mist form, and more active when players are nearby.

text: Which ghost's defining trick is that it can teleport directly next to a random player, leaving EMF readings far from its actual room?
detail: It doesn't walk to you. It just appears.
explain: Wraith teleports adjacent to a random player periodically, generating EMF 2 or 5 readings at the new location. Combined with its salt immunity, far-from-room EMF is a strong Wraith indicator.

text: You suspect this ghost. The hunt rolled into hunting mode the moment three lit candles in a row were blown out.
detail: Flame as trigger, not just deterrent.
explain: Onryo attempts a hunt every time three flames in a row are extinguished. A fourth lit flame in range acts as a one-shot crucifix. Maintain at least three lit candles in its room and don't blow them out yourself.

text: Which two ghosts have hunt thresholds tied to ENVIRONMENTAL conditions rather than just sanity %?
detail: Their hunt window changes based on what's happening around them.
explain: Mare hunts at 60% (lights off) or 40% (lights on). Raiju hunts at 65% (near electronics) or 50% (no electronics). Yokai also shifts based on voice (50% → 80%), but the cleanest pair tied to ENVIRONMENT (not player action) is Mare and Raiju.

text: A ghost that appears as a tall, crawling, or bent-over figure during hunts — is this enough to identify it?
detail: Players sometimes claim the model 'looks like' a specific ghost.
options: No — ghost models are randomly assigned and shared across ALL ghost types
Yes — that's always a Patient 07 form, which is the Shade
Only if the figure is glowing
explain: Ghost models are randomly assigned and shared across all ghost types. The Patient 07 'crawling' model can belong to any ghost. The only model-based exceptions: Banshee and Dayan are always female, so a male model rules them out. Otherwise: appearance tells you nothing.

text: When the ghost interacts with a door, the door fully opens or closes by itself — and the EMF reader picks up TWO separate level-2 readings on that door.
detail: Not a slam, a deliberate movement.
explain: Yurei can fully open or close doors, creating two EMF 2 readings on the door itself. This is one of its core behavioral tells. Pair it with rapid sanity drain through open doors for a confident ID.

text: Two ghosts have a SHORTENED smudge stun versus the standard 90 seconds. Which?
detail: These are the ones where smudging buys you the least time.
options: Demon (60 s) — and that's the only one shortened
explain: Only Demon has a shortened smudge stun at 60 s. Spirit has an EXTENDED stun (180 s), not shortened. All other ghosts use the standard 90 seconds (with Yurei being a special case where it gets trapped in its room for 90 s).

text: The ghost rolled into a hunt while one of your teammates was at a different floor. Your teammate continued investigating, completely unaffected — only one specific player was actually being hunted.
detail: It's narrowly focused.
explain: Banshee targets one player and only that player. Teammates can walk past during a chase and even within line of sight without being killed. Identifying who is being targeted (via crucifix carry, smudge tests) can confirm a Banshee.

text: Yokai's hunt threshold WITHOUT voice activity near it?
detail: Without any voice within 2 m, it acts like a standard ghost.
explain: Yokai defaults to the standard 50% threshold. It only rises to 80% when players speak within 2 m of it. Without voice chat near the ghost, Yokai is indistinguishable from a standard 50% ghost on threshold alone.

text: Which ghost cannot copy evidence — and therefore is identifiable by a 'bonus' fourth evidence type appearing on contract?
detail: It can shapeshift behavior but not evidence.
options: The Mimic — always produces Ghost Orbs in addition to its evidence set
Obake — always produces an extra fingerprint
Twins — produces two of every evidence
Thaye — produces fewer evidences with age
explain: The Mimic's actual evidence is Fingerprints + Spirit Box + Freezing, but it ALWAYS produces Ghost Orbs as a decoy fourth evidence. If orbs appear on a contract where evidence patterns shouldn't include them, suspect Mimic.

text: Looking at the ghost during an event drains sanity TWICE as fast as the standard rate. Which?
detail: Don't make eye contact.
explain: Phantom drains sanity faster than any other ghost when you look at it. Take a photo to make it disappear (the event continues but the visual stops draining sanity), or just look away.

text: Closes doors during hunts and is known for opening/closing them outside of hunts too. Open doors in its room speed up sanity loss.
detail: Door enthusiast.
explain: Yurei is the door ghost — it opens or closes doors during normal play (creating 2× EMF 2 readings), and it accelerates sanity drain via open doors. During hunts it tends to close doors behind it as well.

text: Which ghost type has the SHORTEST hunt cooldown — the least downtime between hunts?
detail: Standard cooldown is 25 seconds.
explain: Demon has the shortest cooldown at 20 s, versus the standard 25 s. Combined with its high 70% threshold and ability to hunt at any sanity, it's the most aggressive ghost on every dimension.

text: Electronics within ~10 m on the same floor start failing during hunts even though the ghost isn't directly interacting with them.
detail: Cameras die, flashlights flicker harder, equipment in the area fails.
explain: Raiju emits electronic interference across a radius that scales with map size (6 m small / 8 m medium / 10 m large) on the same floor. Cameras and flashlights die early during its hunts. Turn off non-essential gear to suppress its 65% threshold bonus.

text: What's the test to identify a Mare reliably WITHOUT waiting for a hunt?
detail: Use its lighting preference.
options: Turn on lights in adjacent rooms but leave one dark — Mare drifts toward unlit room
Photograph it three times in succession
Place a smudge in the favorite room
explain: Mare prefers darkness and will roam toward unlit rooms over lit ones. Setting up a 'light trap' — bright rooms surrounding one dark room — can confirm a Mare without needing to drop sanity into hunt territory.

text: Which ghost's identifying behavior is that it ages over time?
detail: Older = slower, less active.
explain: Thaye ages every 1–2 minutes when a player is in its room (+30 s if empty). Each age increment slows it and lowers its hunt threshold. Its activity drops dramatically over a single contract — early hunts then prolonged silence is the classic Thaye arc.

text: Which ghost is the ONLY one that can hunt the moment you enter the location at 100% sanity, with no setup?
detail: It doesn't need any sanity drain to trigger.
explain: Demon is the only ghost that can attempt a hunt at any sanity level, including 100%. While the probability is low at full sanity, it's nonzero — and combined with the 70% threshold, a Demon can credibly hunt the second you unlock the front door.
